_example._comment: WORKED EXAMPLE — not an active claim. If registered as a claim, the gate BLOCKS it (exit 1): the AER-LIVE-006 mutation. Interval entry [0,0], U*S, bound 5 — the cold engine answers UNRESOLVED (PROVEN_UNBOUNDED peak one-to-infinity, final debt exactly 0). A claim asserting NO_BREACH on final-debt-only evidence {"final_debt": 0} is refused by the independent verifier with FinalDebtOnlyClaimError: the peak is the controlling quantity, and a later service reset never erases a possible earlier breach. This is the exact compliance fraud D61 exists to prevent.

_note: Unbounded-interval compliance claims judged by tools/d61_unbounded_debt_gate.py against the REAL D61 engine (drift_canary/unbounded_debt_bounds.py, PR #2316). Empty 'claims' = explicit DORMANT (never a false green). The first claim merged activates enforcement with zero new wiring. Claims are evidence declarations: the gate rebuilds the interval, contract, and finite limit from the claim's own bytes, cold-assesses with UnboundedDebtEngine.assess, and runs the independent verifier verify_compliance_claim — a claim the law refuses (final-debt-only NO_BREACH, NO_BREACH against an unbounded peak, circular finite limit, inadmissible limit source, receipt-inconsistent claim) is BLOCKED (exit 1); an untrustworthy manifest or a broken engine is BROKEN (exit 2).

_schema.asserts: NO_BREACH | BREACH | UNRESOLVED — what the claim asserts

contract.capacity_basis: the real capacity basis the bound was derived from, not an arbitrary timeout
contract.service_bound_rounds: int > 0 — the bound the peak is judged against
contract.standard: BOUNDED — the law refuses unbounded intervals under any other standard

_schema.evidence: dict naming what the claim rests on, e.g. {"final_debt": 0} or {"finite_limit_source": ..., "max_unserved_rounds": ..., "evidence_ref": ...} or {"peak_witness": {"entry_debt": lo, "unserved_rounds": 0}}
_schema.evidence_ref: link to the evidence (board comment, run log, check run)
_schema.finite_limit: optional — {source, max_unserved_rounds, evidence_ref}; source must be TRUSTED_SEQUENCE_NUMBERS | ENFORCED_RESET | LAW_WITHDRAWAL

interval.entry_debt_lo: int >= 0 — debt interval at the interval's start
interval.must_end_with_service: bool — true = U*S language (valid exit demonstrated), false = U* (no demonstrated exit)

_schema.obligation_id: the scheduling obligation the compliance claim is about (also binds the contract)
_schema.tested_sla_ref: optional — names the SLA under test; required for a finite limit to be accepted (circularity cannot be excluded without it)
